branch_strategy.rule: Do NOT work directly on main. All work happens on a branch off the backup checkpoint.

success_criteria: Truthful UX about what is LIVE vs SCAFFOLD/SHIM/NOT_IMPLEMENTED.
ASF/Abigail/Sentinel still boot cleanly and behave as before.
No secrets or tokens added to git history.
12-department test matrix passes without Abigail claiming fake backend capabilities.

runtime: Abigail container starts and serves on localhost:7070.
Sentinel container is healthy on localhost:9091.
/dashboard serves the real ASF Operator Console.
/intake serves the real ASF Intake Intent Compiler.
/api/intake accepts valid job_order_id + scope_hash payloads and writes audit.
Audit persistence survives restart and normal down/up when named volumes remain.
known_gaps: Dashboard department metrics are scaffolded (derived from buildDepartmentState, not live telemetry).
Department Kill/Restart controls are disabled stubs marked for Sprint 6 (no true process control).
Governance tab describes Department Isolation as 'UI Ready Sprint 6' only.
Intake has many technical fields with no plain-language definitions for non-technical operators.
safety_notes: Admin/demo tokens have been visible in terminal previously. Treat them as non-production and rotate before any public demo.
Do NOT hard-code secrets into any tracked files.

must_remain_true_after_changes: docker compose up still brings up Abigail and Sentinel cleanly.
Dashboard and intake still load and function.

goals.title: Truth badges + footer disclaimer in dashboard
goals.intent: Make the console brutally honest about what is LIVE vs SCAFFOLD/SHIM/NOT_IMPLEMENTED/AUDIT-LOGGED.
requirements: Visually label all major surfaces and key metrics with status badges: LIVE, SCAFFOLD, SHIM, NOT IMPLEMENTED, AUDIT-LOGGED.
Specifically call out that department completion/alignment/token usage/active jobs are scaffolded and NOT live telemetry.
Explicitly label the Audit Tail and Kill Switch as LIVE and AUDIT-LOGGED where appropriate.
Add a single footer line clarifying the mixed state.
Do NOT alter any existing live endpoint wiring (status, sentinel-health, audit-tail, chat, e-brake).
acceptance: An operator can glance once at the dashboard and immediately tell which elements are live vs scaffolded vs shim vs not implemented.
No visual element implies that scaffolded department metrics are live telemetry.

goals.title: Rename department controls from Kill/Restart to Isolate/Reinstate (or hide)
goals.intent: Align wording of department controls with their true capabilities today.
requirements: Locate the Department Operating Surface cards and their action buttons.
Rename labels to 'Isolate Dept' and 'Reinstate Dept', update tooltips to explain governance-state shims pending backend wiring.
Ensure the Governance tab still clearly shows that only the global Kill Switch is live today.
Do NOT claim that any department-level kill/restart actually stops processes.
acceptance: No button or tooltip in the UI uses the words 'Kill' or 'Restart' for departments unless true worker/process control exists.
Governance tab language remains accurate about Department Isolation being UI-only until wired.

goals.title: Add review drawers for departments and agents
goals.intent: Give operators a per-unit explanation surface: what is live vs inferred vs scaffolded for each department and agent.
requirements: In the Departments tab: make each department card clickable or add a 'Review' control that opens a drawer or side panel.
Drawer content: Name, code, lead; what data is LIVE vs SCAFFOLD vs SHIM vs NOT IMPLEMENTED; available actions; 'Next wiring' note.
In the Agents tab: make each agent row open a similar review drawer.
Drawers must not break the existing single-scroll-region model.
acceptance: From a department card or agent row, an operator can open a drawer and quickly see: (a) what is live, (b) what is scaffolded, (c) what actions are real, (d) what is planned.
No drawer claims telemetry is live when it is generated or derived scaffold data.

goals.title: Definition bubbles for technical fields in Intake
goals.intent: Make the 16-section Intent Map usable by non-technical founders by explaining technical choices in plain language.
requirements: Add small '?' help icons or definition bubbles next to highest-risk technical fields.
For each help bubble, answer: 1) What does this mean? 2) Why does Abigail/ASF need it? 3) What happens if I choose this?
Text must be short, non-jargony, and safe to show to a founder/operator audience.
Implementation can be pure HTML/CSS/JS inside intake.html (no new framework).
Respect the existing dark theme/visual style.
acceptance: A non-technical user can read the definition bubble and make a reasonable choice without guessing.

goals.title: 12-department local validation test matrix
goals.intent: Prove that Abigail routes, constrains, and audits correctly per department without hallucinating backend state.
requirements: Define one canonical prompt per department in a test manifest.
Add brief instructions on how to run these prompts locally in the operator chat and verify correct behavior.
Document pass/fail criteria clearly.
acceptance: Running through all 12 prompts locally yields department-appropriate answers without hallucinated backend state.
Any failure mode is easy to spot via the documented criteria.

non_goals: No implementation of real department-level worker kill/restart in this sprint.
No change to core audit-chain cryptography or Sentinel's internal behavior.
No migration to a new UI framework or design system.
